page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance provisioned with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor built on x86_64 architecture, the instance operates at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. Hardware resources include 32 KB L1d cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It uses dedicated CPU allocation and supports vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, along with hardware-assisted cryptographic routines including AES and SHA_NI. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing indicates distinct performance characteristics between single-threaded and parallel computing workloads. Single-core processing demonstrates high efficiency, with single-core stress-ng scores placing in the top tier and single-core Geekbench results reaching 2007.0. Text processing performance is similarly high. Conversely, multi-threaded benchmarks demonstrate lower relative performance output; multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation tasks with Clang, Passmark database operations, static web serving throughput (5.45 GB/sec), and Redis SET operations (5.66 million operations/sec) show weaker comparative placement.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the ecs.r8ae.xlarge centers on its elevated memory density relative to core count. It allows memory-bound applications to run without paying for unused CPU cores. However, the limitation of 2 physical cores and 4 Gbps network bandwidth creates trade-offs for concurrent multi-threaded workloads or high-volume network IOPS. The instance is suited for in-memory caching, text processing engines, database intermediate layers, and memory-intensive applications requiring strong single-thread execution.
